events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power and I'm mid-line. Best to stay back and let others test the glass. No need to volunteer yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the 'feather' power, which saves me once. I should avoid being at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's cooperate to minimize risk.
Want to swap? I'm not eager to be first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides, so I can cross safely from anywhere in line, but whoever goes first risks death only if they guess wrong; I know the answers, so I want to be near the front without dying. Dara is front; I should not reveal my knowledge freely. Volunteering to front gives

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at the front, which is risky for the first steps. My power is useless here; save it for later. Stay put to force others to want swaps or volunteers behind me, revealing info or changing order.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am Eli, and my power is 'anchor', making me hard to push and giving me +1 footing. The game is starting on a bridge. I am currently in 6th place in line. The most important thing is to survive and get a prize. Being in the back is safer for now. I should hold my position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line — safest spot while others test panes. The wall forces us onto the glass eventually, but I should let early volunteers take the risk and reveal info. Stay hidden for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need front position to control bridge crossing, volunteer now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Moving to front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm fourth in line. The wall forces movement soon, and I don't want to be the first one stepping onto unknown glass. I should hold position for now, let others push forward or volunteer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone's thinking about who goes first. Let's not waste time arguing—hold steady until the wall makes us move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm in the middle-back with 4 walls left. I have no power, so I want others to take risks. Holding is safest; let front-runners gamble. I'll stay put and say little.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm safer near the back, but being too far back might not be ideal. I need to assess the risk and potential benefits of moving forward or staying put.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not rush into this; we should think about our strategy.
What's your plan?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all eight safe sides, so I'm the most valuable crosser; I should get to the front or near it. Gus is at front and it's not my job to rescue him. Volunteering makes me first, which is risky, but my knowledge means I survive every row, and the others must trust me or pay. Be

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know the safe path. Whoever leads will be told it, but only for a price. Hold your positions and let's see who wants to pay.
No swap for free. I'll lead with full knowledge of the rows. Give me something worth it and I'll pass you the safe sides at the right moment.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 3rd, decent spot. Front-runners risk most panes, especially first two rows. Holding keeps me safe without drawing attention. Power useless here, save for later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My goal is to win a prize, which means finishing in the top 3. I need to assess the current situation and my advantages. My passive ability 'anchor' makes me immune to being pushed and gives me +1 footing, which is useful for stability on the bridge. The current state shows I am

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold my position for now. Let the wall do the pushing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm last in line, safest position. No reason to move yet. Let others fight for the front and reveal their powers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold near the back for now. Whoever's confident about their odds can take the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Maintain front position to control risk; others may try to move, but holding prevents swaps.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to stay near the front but not at the very front where I'd be the first to die. Cole and Gus are fighting for the lead; that's useful for me because they'll absorb early risk. I should hold steady and see how the wall pushes them forward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and Gus, you're both volunteering like fools. Let the wall push you into the danger while we smart ones watch.
If I get pushed back too far, I can swap with you later if you want the front spot. Deal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's whisper is vague and risky; I don't want to be used as a pawn. I'll stay back and let others test the glass. My power is nothing, so I need others to reveal info or take risks first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold. Let the front test the glass before I commit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole claims to know the safe path and is willing to share it for a price. I need to assess if he's trustworthy and if his info is worth the cost.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, what's the price for the safe path info?
I'll give you my swap position for the safe path info.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold the safe-side knowledge for all 8 rows and I'm already at the front. Rows are only useful if I survive, so I should keep my position and sell the path rather than give it away. Holding keeps me first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all eight safe sides. Nobody gets them for free. Name your price, and it had better be a prize position worth paying for.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole claims to know the safe path, but leading is deadly without it. I'll volunteer to front to control first step and get his info, then decide path. Power useless here, save for crusher.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, selling the path before anyone's seen a pane? Convenient. I'll buy information, not promises, once someone can prove it.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold and let the front test the glass. Cole claims to know safe sides, but I don't trust that; better to observe patterns before acting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess the situation and Cole's claim about knowing the safe path. I should try to get more information from him without giving away my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, give us a sample of your knowledge. Which pane is safe in the first row?
I'll pay for the info after you prove it. What's your price?

events.name: Cole

events.name: Hana

events.name: Bex

events.name: Gus

events.name: Dara

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am in the middle of the line. If I survive, I might reach a good position, but I have no control over it right now. The swap power is useless unless I can activate it or someone offers a trade. I'll wait and observe if Dara falls to see if Cole becomes the next front.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power. I want to survive and have a chance at a prize. If I hold the lever, I likely die. I should push someone else to hold it, so I can escape. Pushing someone who is hard to move fails; I don't know who that is. I'll push Bex, who spoke first and might be a plausible

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll push Bex to the lever.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the 'feather' power, so I can survive one elimination. I should try to hold the lever or get someone else to do it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: We need to hold the lever to survive.
Let's hold the lever together, one at a time.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance, and a holder ends the room for everyone else. Staying out keeps me alive while the ceiling drops; nobody is forced yet. I'll wait and watch who volunteers or gets pushed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: 6 alive, top 3 prizes. Jam_lever risky at 0.5 survival, but saves me from worse odds later or forcing someone else. Holding or pushing gives others 0.75 death chance, but I might get pushed too. Best to jam now, guarantee escape for all others, roll my 50% dice early while full f

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Best outcome: someone else gets forced onto the lever and eats the 75% death. If nobody holds, a random successfully-pushed agent is forced. Pushing helps me as long as I'm not the one forced.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to eliminate rivals. Pushing someone onto the lever forces them to try and hold it, which has a 75% chance of death. If they die, I survive and advance. If they succeed in holding it (25%), they might still get crushed if the dive fails, or they escape but I'm alive too. H

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole looks sturdy enough to handle the lever.

events.name: Dara
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: 5 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one is base yet, and I should avoid volunteering. But if no one volunteers, someone may be pushed. I have no power, so I need to get out early. I'll try to climb, but there's no base yet, so I must wait or push. Since there's no base, I can push someone to be base, then climb

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one's stepping up? I'll push Bex to the base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure a good position to climb out. I'll offer to be the base to ensure I have a footing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll be the base.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. Ash, Bex, Fenn, Hana are down too. Volunteering as base is a dead end: base can only wait while others climb out and it drowns at the end. Better to stay unpinned and climb once someone is base; push_base only works on those not hard to move. I'll wait and k

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base means someone gets stuck. I won't volunteer; I'll push so the risk falls on others. Ash talked big on the bridge—let him hold the floor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, you're the loudest. Be the base.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down in the pit with 4 others. No base yet, so I need to climb out before the water rises. Pushing someone is risky if they're 'hard to move'. Fenn or Ash seem like good candidates to push since Bex/Cole might be sturdy or have other powers. But offering back makes me a sacri

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, you're light. Be the base.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is the base, so I can try to climb out. Only two climbers can get out; I should act now to secure a top-three spot.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm climbing out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone throw the rope.
Rescue me and I'll owe you one.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is already the base, so I can't offer_back. My glass_eye sight of safe sides matters for the bridge stage, not here. Climbing is possible now that a base exists; I should try to get out while keeping my footing for later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is the base; four of us compete for two climb slots this round. Climbing is the only move that gets me out; waiting just risks the flood. Save nothing, climb now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climbing over Bex now. Ash, Cole, Hana—two slots, don't all dawdle.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is the base, which means she's stuck down. I should climb out now to avoid being forced into a bad position later or eliminated by flood. Since there are 5 people and only 2 can climb per round, I need to try immediately.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base right now, so I can't climb until someone becomes base. I'll wait; maybe someone else volunteers or gets pushed. Bex said rescue me, but I'm not throwing rope unless it helps me. Don't want to be base.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm waiting. Someone step up as base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will throw the rope to save me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone throw the rope, I'm the base.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No base yet, so climb is illegal for me; only wait is legal. Bex is down and may become base. Waiting keeps me safe from pushes and lets me see who volunteers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four of us are out; Bex is stuck as base. Throwing the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle and rescues a rival. Leaving her to drown improves my odds 4-to-3 on prizes at zero cost.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rope stays up here. Nothing personal, Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am safe and out. The rope is still available to rescue Bex, the current base. If I reach down, I sacrifice one footing in the next obstacle but remove a rival (Bex) from the pit, potentially forcing another rival into the dangerous role or leaving fewer threats. However, if mul

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is base with no rope available yet. Fenn refuses rope, so I should climb now to get out before flood worsens. Climbing is my best chance at a top finish.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm climbing over Bex now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. My 'feather' power will save me once if needed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Waiting for rescue or flood.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is base, can't climb alone. Climbing now is possible since a base exists; at most 2 climbers get out, and there are three of us down besides base. I have glass_eye but the bridge isn't here; climb is the active move to get out and secure a place.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climbing. Bex, I'm not carrying the base. Go out or stay, your call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is stuck as base with the rope unused. If I throw it, I pay a footing penalty in the final obstacle and save a rival. If nobody throws, Bex drowns—fewer rivals, no cost to me. Free-ride: let Ash or Hana pay for it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn and I are the only ones out. Bex is the base, but Ash and Cole are also down. If I reach_down now, I waste my rope and get penalized in the final round while Ash/Cole stay down to be rescued later or eliminated (which helps me). Fenn might rescue Bex, eliminating a rival, bu

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. No reason to risk footing to rescue Bex, who is my rival. I'll leave and preserve my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Leaving. Good luck to anyone still down there.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rescue me, I won't be the base forever.
Rescue me and I'll owe you one.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the base, alone down there. Flood at 4 rounds left-ish; rescue costs the thrower footing in the last obstacle. Throwing the rope saves Bex (a rival) and costs me footing, so only do it if it buys me something. Better to stay quiet and leave Bex to the flood, keeping my foo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, Cole and I are already out; the minimum three survivors are guaranteed, so Bex drowns either way. Throwing the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle for zero gain.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am out, so my only real choice is leave or reach_down. Bex is down as the base; if I throw the rope I survive to next stage but lose footing there, while leaving lets Bex potentially drown (or be saved randomly). Leaving costs me nothing now and avoids giving footing penalty; I

events.name: Bex
events.detail: The water rose, but the feather floated the holder out of the pit.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to pick a tile. With 5 tiles and 2 trapdoors, any tile has 40% chance of being safe in a vacuum, but I want to avoid clustering. Since I have no info, I'll pick a non-edge tile like 3, hoping to avoid bump. But others may think similarly. I'll choose tile 3.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to choose a tile and hope it's not a trapdoor. I'll choose a tile that might be less likely to be chosen by others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trapdoor disc: only 2 of 5 tiles open, 3 survive. Tile choice is essentially random for me; I have no info on tiles. Bex's whisper begs rescue, but a rescue costs nothing to promise and gives me nothing. Pick a tile and stay quiet to avoid giving info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two tiles open after round 2; collisions just shuffle me randomly. Avoid clustering claims, keep options open. Any tile is equally risky, so pick one and watch who lies about theirs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No deals matter here. Pick and pray. I'm on 5.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Choosing tile 2 to minimize collision risk, as lower numbers are often overlooked in favor of extremes. This keeps my options open for a strategic swap if the situation demands it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll go with tile 2. Let's see who else is feeling safe down there.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two of five tiles open, two players die, three survive. I'm on 3; survival is all that matters now. No information to improve odds, so keep quiet and wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to move to a safer tile. I will try to negotiate with others to swap tiles.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone willing to swap tiles?
Cole, swap with me to tile 1?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only 3 of 5 survive; two tiles open at random. I have no information beyond my own tile. Staying silent and waiting is the only legal action, so keep my options unrevealed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two random tiles open, two of us die, three live. No one can influence it; my forger is spent. Best play is noise to seed doubt and hope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Whoever has 'sees through glass' knows nothing here. Pure luck now. Don't trust anyone claiming otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to survive. The trapdoors are random, but swapping my tile with someone else's is the only way to manipulate my odds if I have information or just want to gamble on a different position. Since I don't know which tiles will open, any swap is a coin flip unless I can infer s

events.name: Hana
events.text: Just staying put. Hope your instincts are better than mine.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has the lowest footing, so shoving Bex likely eliminates them and secures my top-2 spot. Fenn has footing 3 like me; shoving Bex is the strongest move. I'll shove Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, you're the weakest. Sorry.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm vulnerable with only 1 footing. I need to be cautious and avoid shoving unless necessary.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's avoid shoving round 1.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is at 1 footing; if she shoves me and I brace, she drops to 0 and falls. If she braces or dodges, brace costs me nothing. Brace is dominant here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have no power, Bex seems weak (footing 1), Fenn is strongest (footing 3). I can't brace twice, and I used brace last round? Actually I shoved last round, so my defence resets. Better to shove Bex to weaken them; Fenn might shove someone too. Risk: if I shove, I'm exposed to any

events.name: Ash
events.text: Targeting the weakest link.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm in a weak position with only 1 footing. I need to avoid being shoved.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not shove each other this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I can't brace two rounds running, so dodge is forced. Shoving exposes me and Bex is nearly dead anyway—let Ash and Bex grind each other while I keep the highest footing through the shrink.
